# Results {#sec-results}

## 2-variable visualisations

### Population simulation

```{r}
#| label: fig-pop2-ind-plot
#| fig-cap: "Mosaic plot showing the intersection of age and tenure categories when they are generated independently, with age brackets on the x-axis and tenure categories on the y-axis and fill."
# source() only suppresses console output for print.eval-gated
# top-level expressions; simdata2.R's str() calls write directly to
# the console regardless, so capture.output() is used to discard
# everything the sourced script prints, leaving only pop2_ind_plot
# itself to render below.
invisible(capture.output(source("scripts/simdata2.R")))

pop2_ind_plot
```

@fig-pop2-ind-plot shows the intersectional proportions of the age and tenure categories for the independently generated population. There is skew towards upper middle age and higher frequency of homeowners (compared to other categories), but no visible association between categories. As such, the probability of any intersection is explained purely by the margins.

```{r}
#| label: fig-pop2-cov-plot
#| fig-cap: "Mosaic plot showing the intersection of age and tenure categories when they are generated with a negative association between age and renting. Age brackets shown on the x-axis and tenure categories on the y-axis and fill."
# source() only suppresses console output for print.eval-gated
# top-level expressions; simdata2.R's str() calls write directly to
# the console regardless, so capture.output() is used to discard
# everything the sourced script prints, leaving only pop2_ind_plot
# itself to render below.
invisible(capture.output(source("scripts/simdata2.R")))

pop2_cov_plot
```

@fig-pop2-cov-plot shows the intersectional proportions of the age and tenure categories for the population generated with association. There is skew towards upper middle age and higher frequency of homeowners (compared to other categories), and visible negative association between age and renting. The probability of an indivual renting in this population decreases as age increases.

### Sample construction

```{r}
#| label: fig-pop2-ind-slice-plot
#| fig-cap: "Mosaic plot showing the intersection of age and tenure categories when they are generated independently for a 10000-individual slice. Age brackets shown on the x-axis and tenure categories on the y-axis and fill. Structure is preserved."
# source() only suppresses console output for print.eval-gated
# top-level expressions; simdata2.R's str() calls write directly to
# the console regardless, so capture.output() is used to discard
# everything the sourced script prints, leaving only pop2_ind_plot
# itself to render below.
invisible(capture.output(source("scripts/simsamp2.R")))

pop2_ind_slice_plot
```

@fig-pop2-ind-slice-plot shows a random 10% (10000-individual) slice of the independent population, replicating the mailout process of expressions of interest. The independent structure is largely preserved, with very slight deviations in younger and older "Other Tenure" proportions.

```{r}
#| label: fig-pop2-cov-slice-plot
#| fig-cap: "Mosaic plot showing the intersection of age and tenure categories when they are generated with a negative association between age and renting for a 10000-individual slice. Age brackets shown on the x-axis and tenure categories on the y-axis and fill. Structure is preserved."
# source() only suppresses console output for print.eval-gated
# top-level expressions; simdata2.R's str() calls write directly to
# the console regardless, so capture.output() is used to discard
# everything the sourced script prints, leaving only pop2_ind_plot
# itself to render below.
invisible(capture.output(source("scripts/simsamp2.R")))

pop2_cov_slice_plot
```

@fig-pop2-cov-slice-plot shows a random 10% (10000-individual) slice of the associated population, replicating the mailout process of expressions of interest. The associated structure is preserved in the slice.
